mainTopic: Breached fences and פרוץ כעומד, the משנה of rope and reed partitions, and how much space an individual or a caravan may enclose
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of who wrote a ברייתא about breached fences. אביי says all of it follows the רבנן, and רבא says all of it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא that seems to refute רב פפא's view that a breach equal to the standing part (פרוץ כעומד) is permitted. Even so, the הלכה follows רב פפא, because a precise reading of the משנה supports him. A new משנה follows. It teaches that a camp may be fenced with stacked ropes or upright reeds, as long as the gaps are under three טפחים. It also brings disputes over whether this works only for a שיירא and whether a fence needs both שתי וערב. In the גמרא, רב המנונא asks whether 'more standing than open' works for a sideways fence. אביי's attempted proof is rejected, and the question is reframed. Finally, the גמרא sorts out how much space an individual and a caravan may enclose. רב נחמן publicly retracts a ruling and concludes that three people, as a שיירא, get all the space they need.

steps.title: The latter clause seems to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The סֵיפָא treats three-to-four טְפָחִים as its own category. That only makes sense according to רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, who says gaps under four are לָבוּד. So the בָּרַיְיתָא seems split between two authors.
steps.simpleTranslation: So now we have reached the view of רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, who says a gap of less than four is לָבוּד. Because if this followed the רַבָּנַן, why list 'from three to four' separately? For them, three and four are the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second half of the בָּרַיְיתָא matches רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, even though the first half matched the רַבָּנַן. This creates a problem: one teaching seems to have two different authors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רַבָּנַן, לָבוּד stops at three טְפָחִים, so any gap of three or more is simply open. They would have no reason to treat three-to-four as a separate case. Only רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, for whom לָבוּד reaches up to four, has a reason to single out that range.

keyTerms.meaning: We have arrived at (the view of...)
'Joined': a small gap is treated as if it were closed
It is one and the same

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רַבָּנַן reject לָבוּד completely. They agree to it, but only for gaps of less than three. The argument is only about how far לָבוּד reaches: up to three, or up to four.

phrases.english: We have arrived at Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
phrases.notes: Said about the סיפא of the ברייתא

phrases.english: who said: less than four is lavud (considered joined).
For if it were the Rabbis,
why list 'from three until four' separately?
Three and four are one and the same (for them).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָאן לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier analysis (on the previous amud), which showed that the רֵישָׁא follows the רַבָּנַן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the בָּרַיְיתָא has a single author
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רֵישָׁא fits the רַבָּנַן (לָבוּד only below three), but the סֵיפָא's separate three-to-four category only fits רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל. That leaves a split בָּרַיְיתָא.

steps.title: אביי: the whole ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אַבָּיֵי says both clauses follow the רַבָּנַן. Even the רַבָּנַן agree that a standing section counts as significant enough to permit sowing opposite it only if it is four טְפָחִים wide. That is why three-to-four is a separate category.
steps.simpleTranslation: אַבָּיֵי said: since the first clause follows the רַבָּנַן, the second clause also follows the רַבָּנַן. The רַבָּנַן agree that whenever the question is about permitting sowing opposite a standing section, it counts as significant if it is four wide, and does not count if it is less.
steps.whatsHappening: אַבָּיֵי resolves the problem by keeping the whole בָּרַיְיתָא with the רַבָּנַן. He explains the three-to-four category with a different rule that has nothing to do with לָבוּד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סֵיפָא is not about whether a gap is closed by לָבוּד. It is about whether a standing piece of fence is important enough to permit sowing a different species opposite it. For that question, even the רַבָּנַן require a width of four, so the difference between three and four really matters.

phrases.english: Abaye said: since the first clause is the Rabbis,
the latter clause is also the Rabbis.
And the Rabbis agree that for anything meant to permit (sowing) opposite it:
if there is an area of four, it is significant;
and if not, it is not significant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִדְּרֵישָׁא רַבָּנַן, סֵיפָא נָמֵי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem of the split בָּרַיְיתָא from step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the סֵיפָא as following a different rule (a significance requirement), so it fits the רַבָּנַן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three-to-four category must be about לָבוּד, so it must follow רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.terutzMaskana: The three-to-four category is about whether a standing section is significant enough to permit sowing opposite it, and the רַבָּנַן agree to that four-טְפָחִים rule

steps.title: רבא: the whole ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רָבָא says both clauses follow רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל. His four-טְפָחִים לָבוּד applies only to a gap up high. A gap near the ground is like a fence that young goats can slip through, so it is not לָבוּד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רָבָא said: since the latter clause follows רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, the first clause also follows him. When רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל said we apply לָבוּד, that is only for a gap up high. Down below, it is like a fence that young goats break through, and there we do not say לָבוּד.
steps.whatsHappening: רָבָא gives a second, opposite answer: he puts the whole בָּרַיְיתָא with רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל. He explains that the רֵישָׁא's lower limit of three applies because that gap is at ground level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רֵישָׁא, which only treats gaps under three as closed, seemed to fit the רַבָּנַן alone. רָבָא explains that even רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל limits his four-טְפָחִים לָבוּד to gaps that are off the ground. A gap at ground level of three or more lets small animals pass through, so it cannot be treated as closed.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that young goats pass through

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opposite ways to make the בָּרַיְיתָא consistent. אַבָּיֵי: all of it is the רַבָּנַן, and the four-טְפָחִים rule is about significance for permitting sowing. רָבָא: all of it is רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, but his לָבוּד up to four applies only up high, not at ground level.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Rava said: since the latter clause is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: the first clause is also Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אָמְרִינַן לָבוּד —
phrases.english: And when Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said that we apply lavud,
that applies only above (off the ground);
but below (near the ground),

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּמְחִיצָה שֶׁהַגְּדָיִים בּוֹקְעִין בָּהּ —
phrases.english: it is like a partition that young goats break through,
(and there) we do not say lavud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same problem from step 1. It is the opposite of אַבָּיֵי's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל's לָבוּד (above versus below), so the רֵישָׁא also fits him
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רֵישָׁא's three-טְפָחִים limit can only follow the רַבָּנַן
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל does not apply לָבוּד at ground level, where goats can pass through

steps.title: A new ברייתא about walls made mostly of doors and windows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier argument about a breach equal to the standing part (פָּרוּץ כְּעוֹמֵד). It quotes a בָּרַיְיתָא: walls made mostly of doorways and windows are permitted, as long as the standing part is more than the breached part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: walls like these, where most of them are doorways and windows, are permitted, as long as the standing part is more than the breached part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof for the earlier argument about whether a breach equal to the standing part is allowed. It quotes the בָּרַיְיתָא here and will analyze it in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'as long as the standing part is more than the breached part' seem to imply that an equal breach would not be allowed. This would bear on the earlier argument about פָּרוּץ כְּעוֹמֵד. There is also a puzzle: the walls are mostly openings, yet the standing part must be the majority. The גמרא works this out next.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof from a source)
The standing part is more than the breached part

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the setup. The proof and its conclusion come next, so do not draw the final conclusion yet.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
these walls, where most of them are doorways and windows,

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא עוֹמֵד מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפָּרוּץ.
phrases.english: it is permitted, as long as the standing part is more than the breached part.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּפָנוֹת הַלָּלוּ שֶׁרוּבָּן פְּתָחִים וְחַלּוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of the בָּרַיְיתָא's author and returns to the earlier argument about פָּרוּץ כְּעוֹמֵד
steps.raayaObject: Whether a breach equal to the standing part is permitted (פָּרוּץ כְּעוֹמֵד)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A בָּרַיְיתָא about walls made mostly of doorways and windows, which requires the standing part to be the majority

steps.title: The ברייתא's word 'most' cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the ברייתא's wording 'שרובן', meaning most of the wall is doorways and windows. That wording contradicts the ברייתא's own condition that the standing part must be greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Most of them'? Can you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted. If most of the wall is openings, then the standing part cannot be bigger than the open part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the walls are 'mostly' doorways and windows. Yet it also requires the standing part to be greater than the breached part. Both cannot be true at once, so the wording must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (an expression of disbelief)

phrases.english: 'That most of them' — can that enter your mind?!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's own condition (standing must be greater) rules this out.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: 'most are openings' cannot fit with 'the standing part is greater'

steps.title: Correcting the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread as 'שריבה', meaning one added many doorways and windows. The area is permitted as long as the standing part is still greater than the breached part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: if one added many doorways and windows to the walls, it is permitted, provided that the standing part is greater than the breached part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא. It does not mean 'most of the wall is openings.' It means 'many openings were added.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing one word (רובן to ריבה) removes the contradiction. Now the ברייתא clearly teaches that the standing part must be bigger than the open part. This sets up the inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The standing part is greater than the breached part

phrases.english: Rather: to which one added many
phrases.notes: The corrected reading

phrases.english: doorways and windows — it is permitted,
provided that the standing part
is greater than the breached part.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: שֶׁרִיבָּה בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5 by changing the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא said most of the wall is openings
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means many openings were added, and the standing part is still greater

steps.title: The corrected ברייתא seems to refute רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: From 'the standing part must be greater,' the גמרא infers that if the breach equals the standing part, carrying is forbidden. That contradicts רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if the standing part equals the breached part, it is forbidden. This is a refutation of רב פפא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the corrected ברייתא and uses it to attack רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא held that פרוץ כעומד (breach equal to standing) is permitted. The ברייתא requires the standing part to be bigger, so an equal split would be forbidden. That directly contradicts רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who permits פרוץ כעומד

phrases.english: This implies: if it is equal to the breached part, it is forbidden,
a refutation of Rav Pappa!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כַּפָּרוּץ אָסוּר, תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected ברייתא from Step 6 against רב פפא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that פרוץ כעומד is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inference from the ברייתא: requiring 'more standing' implies that an equal split is forbidden

steps.title: רב פפא is refuted, yet the הלכה follows him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רב פפא is refuted. Yet it surprisingly rules like him anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed a refutation. And yet the הלכה follows רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the refutation but still decides the הלכה like רב פפא. This surprising ruling sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when an אמורא is refuted, the הלכה does not follow him. Here the גמרא says both things at once. That creates a puzzle that needs explaining.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'תיובתא' means the הלכה is automatically against him. Here the גמרא deliberately says both: refuted, but the הלכה is still like him.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.
phrases.notes: The גמרא concedes the point

phrases.english: And the הלכה is like Rav Pappa.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא. וְהִילְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the refutation from Step 7 but rules for רב פפא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא is refuted by the ברייתא, but in practice the הלכה follows him

steps.title: How can he be both refuted and the הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions how a refuted view can still be the practical הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A refutation, and yet the הלכה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own ruling from the previous step. It seems strange to rule like someone who was just refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא normally knocks out a position completely. Ruling like that same position seems to contradict that, so the גמרא demands an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation and the הלכה (at once)

phrases.english: A refutation, and the הלכה?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא וְהִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling like רב פפא despite the תיובתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A refuted view normally cannot be the הלכה

steps.title: The משנה's precise wording supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: Yes, the ruling stands, because a careful reading of the משנה supports רב פפא. The משנה says breaches may not be greater than the built part, which implies an equal breach is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, because our משנה, read carefully, supports him. As we learned: 'There may not be breaches greater than the built part.' This implies that if they are equal to the built part, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we rule like רב פפא. A careful reading of the משנה backs him up, even though a ברייתא goes against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implies 'equal is forbidden,' but the משנה implies 'equal is permitted.' A משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא, so the הלכה follows the view the משנה supports. That view is רב פפא's.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Breaches greater than the built part

steps.whatToRemember: פרוץ כעומד (a breach equal to the standing part) is permitted. The הלכה follows רב פפא because the משנה's wording supports him, even though a ברייתא refutes him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a precise inference from a משנה can outweigh a refutation from a ברייתא when deciding practical הלכה.

phrases.english: Yes, because it is precisely implied by
our משנה, in line with him.
As we learned: there may not be breaches
phrases.notes: Quoting the earlier משנה

phrases.english: greater than the built part.
This implies: if equal to the built part, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, מִשּׁוּם דְּדַיְיקָא מַתְנִיתִין כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Support from a precise reading of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A refuted opinion cannot be the הלכה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's wording implies an equal breach is permitted, so the הלכה follows רב פפא

steps.title: New משנה: a partition made of three ropes
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that one may enclose an area with three ropes, one above the other, as long as the gap between each rope and the next is less than three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may surround an area with three ropes, one above the other, and another above that, provided that between one rope and the next there are not three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that ropes stacked close together can count as a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ropes work because gaps under three טפחים are treated as closed (לבוד). If any gap reaches three טפחים, the rope partition fails.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One surrounds with three ropes
one above the other,
and another above that one,
provided that there will not be
three טפחים between one rope and the next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַקִּיפִין שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the פרוץ כעומד discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three stacked ropes form a valid partition, provided that no gap between ropes is three טפחים

steps.title: The ropes must be thick enough to reach ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that the three ropes together must be more than a טפח thick, so the whole fence reaches ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The total thickness of the ropes must be more than one handbreadth, so that everything together comes to ten handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rule about the three-rope fence. It now tells us how thick the ropes must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three gaps: ground to rope 1, rope 1 to rope 2, and rope 2 to rope 3. Each gap must be less than three טפחים, so all three gaps together come to just under nine. The ropes must therefore add up to more than one טפח, so the fence reaches the required ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten handbreadths, the minimum height of a valid מחיצה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ropes alone must be ten טפחים tall. The ten includes the empty gaps between the ropes. The ropes only need to fill in the extra bit beyond the gaps.

phrases.english: The measure of the ropes and their thickness
is more than a handbreadth,
phrases.notes: Combined thickness of all three ropes

phrases.english: so that the whole thing will be ten handbreadths.
phrases.notes: The gaps (each just under 3) plus the ropes reach 10

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁיעוּר חֲבָלִים וְעוֹבְיָין יָתֵר עַל טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a measurement detail to the three-rope rule in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ropes together must be more than a טפח thick, so the fence including its gaps reaches ten טפחים.

steps.title: A fence of upright reeds
steps.stepSummary: Instead of sideways ropes, one may surround the area with upright reeds, as long as no gap between two reeds is three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may surround the area with reeds, as long as there are not three handbreadths between one reed and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second option. Instead of a fence of sideways ropes, you can stand reeds upright around the area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ropes run sideways, and reeds stand up and down, but the same principle works for both. A gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed (this is the idea of לבוד). So a row of reeds with small gaps counts as a solid wall.

phrases.english: One may surround with reeds,
phrases.notes: Standing upright, the opposite direction of the ropes

phrases.english: as long as there will not be
three handbreadths between one reed and the next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקִּיפִין בְּקָנִים, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין קָנֶה לַחֲבֵירוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an upright version of the sideways rope fence from steps 11 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upright reeds with gaps of less than three טפחים form a valid enclosure.

steps.title: Only for a caravan, or for everyone?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says these light fences were allowed only for a שיירא. The חכמים say the caravan was mentioned only because it was the common case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They spoke of a caravan only. This is the view of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: they did not mean only a caravan. They spoke of what usually happens.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a disagreement about who may use these rope and reed fences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says this lenient kind of fence is only for a caravan, because travelers can't build a real wall. Everyone else needs a full מחיצה. The חכמים say the rule works for everyone. The caravan was mentioned only because travelers were the people who usually made such fences.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a common idea across ש"ס: a case mentioned in a משנה may be only the typical example (דיבר הכתוב בהווה), not a real limit on the law.

phrases.english: They spoke about a caravan,
phrases.notes: Meaning: only a caravan

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
But the Sages say:
They did not speak of a caravan specifically, but of the usual case.
phrases.notes: The law applies to everyone

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁיָירָא דִּבְּרוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who may use the rope and reed fences described in steps 11 to 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה limits these fences to a caravan. The חכמים allow them for everyone.

steps.title: Must a fence have both upright and sideways parts?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a fence needs both upright and sideways parts (שתי וערב). The חכמים say one of the two is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any partition that is not made of both upright and sideways parts is not a partition. This is the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The חכמים say: one of the two is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a second disagreement. This one is about whether ropes alone or reeds alone are enough to make a fence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is the strictest view. Ropes alone or reeds alone are never a מחיצה, not even for a caravan. You need both together, like threads woven into cloth. The חכמים say either direction alone works, which matches the simple rules in steps 11 to 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Warp and woof: up-and-down plus side-to-side parts, like woven cloth
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה
One of the two things (either one is enough)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on a light fence of ropes or reeds. The חכמים say it works for everyone. רבי יהודה says it works only for a caravan. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, in the simple reading, says it never works unless it has both upright and sideways parts (step 34 narrows this to giving כל צרכן).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי יהודה (step 14) with his son רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (this step). They hold different views. The father allows a one-direction fence for a caravan. In the simple reading of the משנה, the son allows it for no one (step 34 limits this to giving כל צרכן).

phrases.english: Any partition that is not
made of warp and of woof,
phrases.notes: Both upright and sideways parts

phrases.english: is not a partition,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
But the Sages say:
One of the two things is enough.
phrases.notes: Either upright or sideways alone

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מְחִיצָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל שְׁתִי וְשֶׁל עֵרֶב אֵינָהּ מְחִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter view than רבי יהודה's in step 14. It questions whether a fence built in only one direction works at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires both upright and sideways parts. The חכמים accept either one alone.

steps.title: For upright reeds, more standing than open counts as a wall
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes רב: in a fence made of upright pieces (שתי), if the standing part is greater than the open part, the fence counts as standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב המנונא said in the name of רב: They said that with upright pieces (שתי), if the standing part is more than the open part, it counts as standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens on the משנה with a rule from רב. A fence of upright reeds counts as a real wall when the solid part is bigger than the open part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הרי אמרו' refer back to the earlier משנה about fences, where 'standing more than open' was taught. רב tells us that this rule clearly applies to upright pieces (שתי). This sets up the question in the next step about sideways pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: The standing (solid) part is greater than the open (breached) part
Warp: upright, vertical pieces of a fence, like reeds stuck in the ground
'Behold, they said': pointing back to an established teaching
It counts as standing, a valid wall

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Hamnuna said that Rav said:
Behold, they said:
phrases.notes: Refers to the earlier משנה about fences

phrases.english: if the standing part is greater than the open part with upright pieces
it counts as standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר רַב: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by stating the known rule for upright fences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a fence of upright pieces (שתי), if the standing part is greater than the open part, the fence is valid.

steps.title: What about a fence of sideways ropes?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks whether the same rule applies to a fence made only of sideways pieces (ערב).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא asked: With sideways pieces (ערב), what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא asks a real question. Does 'more standing than open' also work for a fence made of horizontal ropes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the rule works for upright reeds. Horizontal ropes might be different, because the gaps run the full length of the fence. The question is whether the rule extends to ערב.

keyTerms.meaning: Woof: horizontal, sideways pieces of a fence, like ropes

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna asked:
With sideways pieces, what is the rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule just stated for שתי extends to ערב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'standing more than open' make a fence of only horizontal pieces valid?

steps.title: אביי's proof from the rope thickness rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings the משנה's rule that the ropes must total more than a טפח thick. If 'more standing than open' worked for ropes, that requirement would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear: 'The measure of the ropes and their thickness must be more than a טפח, so that the whole fence is ten טפחים.' And if it were so (that the rule works for ערב), why would I need more than a טפח?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to answer רב המנונא's question from the wording of our משנה. He suggests that the answer is 'no' for sideways ropes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה demands that the three ropes together be more than a טפח thick. If 'more standing than open' worked for ropes, we could get away with thinner ropes, so the extra thickness would be pointless. Since the משנה demands it, the rule must not apply to ערב.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an introduction to a proof from a source
The measure of the ropes and their thickness
And if it were so: 'if your idea were true'

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיעוּר חֲבָלִים וְעוֹבְיָין יָתֵר עַל טֶפַח,
phrases.english: the measure of the ropes and their thickness must be more than a handbreadth,
so that the whole fence will be ten handbreadths.
And if it were so (that the rule works for sideways pieces),
why do I need more than a handbreadth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve רב המנונא's question using the משנה from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That 'standing more than open' does NOT validate a fence of sideways ropes (ערב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's requirement that the ropes total more than a טפח thick.

steps.title: The cheaper fence that would work if the rule applied
steps.stepSummary: אביי spells out the alternative: three thin ropes spaced so that two gaps are under three טפחים and one gap is under four. This would make the solid part bigger than the open part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him make: less than three, and a thin rope; less than three, and a thin rope; less than four, and a thin rope.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his proof by showing exactly how someone could build a valid ten-טפח fence with very thin ropes, if the rule applied to ערב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gaps under three טפחים count as closed because of לבוד. So the two small gaps plus their ropes make about six 'standing' טפחים, against one open gap of about four. Standing would outnumber open, so thick ropes would not be needed. The משנה still requires them, which supports אביי's point.

keyTerms.meaning: A rope of any thickness, even very thin
Less than three טפחים: a gap considered closed by לבוד

steps.confusionAlert: The two gaps under three טפחים are not counted as 'open.' Because of לבוד they count as solid wall. Only the gap of nearly four טפחים is open, so about six solid טפחים outweigh four open ones.

phrases.english: Let him make a gap of less than three, and a rope of any size,
a gap of less than three, and a rope of any size,
a gap of less than four, and a rope of any size.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶיעְבֵּיד פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה וְחֶבֶל מַשֶּׁהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's proof by describing the alternative fence that would make the משנה's rule unnecessary.
steps.raayaObject: The thick-rope requirement only makes sense if ערב cannot use 'standing more than open.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A thin-rope fence of about six solid טפחים to four open would otherwise be enough.

steps.title: Where would the four-handbreadth gap go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions אביי's alternative fence. If the nearly four-טפח gap is placed at the bottom, the fence is one that goats can pass through, which is invalid anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think so? Where would he place this 'less than four' gap? If he places it at the bottom, it is like a fence that goats pass through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof by asking whether his thin-rope fence could ever work. It checks the first placement option, the bottom. Steps 21 and 22 test the top and middle placements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the alternative fence fails for a different reason, the משנה's thick-rope requirement proves nothing about ערב. A gap near the ground that goats can slip through ruins a fence no matter how much is standing above it. So the bottom placement does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And can you understand it so?': a challenge to the reasoning just given
A fence that young goats pass through: invalid as a wall

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a fence's validity depends not only on the ratio of solid to open, but also on where the gap is. An opening at ground level can disqualify the whole fence.

phrases.english: And can you really think so?

phrases.aramaic: הַאי פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבָּעָה הֵיכָא מוֹקֵים לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: This 'less than four' gap, where does he place it?
If he places it at the bottom,

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּמְחִיצָה שֶׁהַגְּדָיִים בּוֹקְעִין בָּהּ.
phrases.english: it is like a fence that goats pass through.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיסְבְּרָא? הַאי פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבָּעָה הֵיכָא מוֹקֵים לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternative fence on which אביי's proof depends.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Targets אביי's proof (steps 18-19), not the underlying question. The rejection is still in progress, since only the bottom placement has been examined so far.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The alternative fence may be invalid for an independent reason. A low gap is a fence 'that goats pass through,' so the משנה's thick-rope rule may not prove anything about ערב.

steps.title: Placing the big gap at the top also fails
steps.stepSummary: If the nearly four-טפח gap is put at the top, the top rope is cancelled by the open air above and below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he places it (the big gap) at the top, the open air on this side and on that side comes and cancels it (the top rope).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps testing אביי's imagined rope fence. Now it tries putting the big gap at the top and shows that this fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top rope sits alone. Above it is open sky, and below it is a gap of almost four טפחים. That gap is too wide for the ropes to count as joined. With open air on both sides, the lone top rope is cancelled, and the fence is no longer ten טפחים tall.

phrases.english: If he places it (the big gap) at the top,
phrases.notes: Second possible placement of the nearly-four-טפח gap.

phrases.english: the air of this side (above the top rope) comes
phrases.notes: The open sky above the fence.

phrases.english: and of that side (the gap below), and cancels it.
phrases.notes: The top rope is surrounded by open space and loses its status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מוֹקֵים לֵיהּ עִילַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rejection begun in step 20 by testing the second possible placement of the gap.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the top placement of the large gap in אביי's imagined fence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The top rope is isolated by air above and a wide gap below, so it is cancelled.

steps.title: Placing the big gap in the middle raises a different, unresolved question
steps.stepSummary: With the gap in the middle, the standing part is only bigger when both sides are added together. If such a fence counted, it would settle a question that the גמרא never resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he places it in the middle, then the standing part is bigger than the open part only from two sides together. Then you could learn from this that standing that is bigger than open from two sides counts as standing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option, putting the big gap in the middle. It shows that this turns into a completely different question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side of the middle gap is bigger than the gap on its own. Only the two sides added together beat the open part. Whether that kind of combined count works was itself left unresolved. So אביי's proof cannot rely on it, because then the משנה would be settling that open question.

keyTerms.meaning: From two sides (standing parts combined from both sides of the gap)
You can learn from this (here used to show an unacceptable result)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'שמעת מינה' here is NOT a real conclusion. It is said with surprise, meaning: 'Would you really prove that unresolved question from here?' It closes off the last option for אביי's proof.

phrases.english: If he places it (the big gap) in the middle,
phrases.notes: Third and final placement option.

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ עוֹמֵד מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפָּרוּץ
phrases.english: then it is a case of standing greater than open
only from two sides (combined).
phrases.notes: Each side alone is smaller than the gap.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ עוֹמֵד מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפָּרוּץ
phrases.english: Then you would learn from this that standing greater than open
phrases.notes: Said in surprise, meaning: that cannot be right.

phrases.english: from two sides counts as standing!
phrases.notes: That question is left unresolved elsewhere, so it cannot be proven here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מוֹקֵים לֵיהּ בְּמִיצְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-way test (bottom, top, middle) and knocks down אביי's alternative fence completely.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the middle placement, and with it, אביי's whole proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The middle placement depends on the unresolved 'two sides' question, so it cannot prove anything.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since every placement fails, אביי's proof from the משנה collapses. That forces the גמרא to rethink what רב המנונא was actually asking.

steps.title: Reframing רב המנונא's question as a mat with a hole
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא's real question is about a mat a little over seven טפחים tall, with a three-טפח hole cut in it, placed less than three טפחים off the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רב המנונא was asking: for example, someone brought a mat of seven טפחים and a bit, cut a three-טפח hole in it, left four טפחים and a bit, and set it up less than three טפחים from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the rope cases did not work, the גמרא redefines רב המנונא's question with a new case that avoids all the earlier problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mat stands less than three טפחים off the ground, so the bottom gap counts as closed (לבוד). That makes the fence ten טפחים tall, and goats cannot get through. The three-טפח hole is the open part, and the solid part of the mat is bigger. So the question is now clean: does 'more standing than open' work for this kind of horizontal setup?

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny bit, any small amount
Less than three טפחים (the range where a gap counts as closed, לבוד)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַב הַמְנוּנָא הָכִי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what Rav Hamnuna was asking:
phrases.notes: Introduces a new understanding of the question from step 17.

phrases.english: for example, where someone brought a mat
that is seven (handbreadths) and a bit,
and cut a three-handbreadth hole in it,
phrases.notes: Three is not 'less than three', so the hole counts as open.

phrases.english: and left four (handbreadths) and a bit (solid),
phrases.notes: The solid part is bigger than the hole.

phrases.english: and set it up less than three (handbreadths) off the ground.
phrases.notes: The bottom gap counts as closed (לבוד), so the total height is ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַב הַמְנוּנָא הָכִי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the failure of אביי's proof by redefining the original question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא of the question)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב המנונא asked about a horizontal fence of ropes. But no rope arrangement gives a clean test case: a bottom gap lets goats through, a top gap cancels the top rope, and a middle gap turns into the unresolved 'two sides' question.
steps.terutzMaskana: He asked about a specific mat case that avoids the goat problem and the 'two sides' problem, so the משנה does not settle it.

steps.title: רב אשי: the question was about a hanging partition
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a different explanation: רב המנונא was asking about a partition that hangs in the air and does not reach the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He was asking about a hanging partition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second, different way to understand רב המנונא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's view, the issue is not the ratio of open to standing. It is a partition that hangs above the ground and does not reach it. This sets up the next step, which brings a parallel question about exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging partition that does not reach the ground
He was asking (this was his question)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
phrases.notes: Attribution, merged into this step.

phrases.english: He was asking about a hanging partition.
phrases.notes: A new understanding of רב המנונא's question.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה אִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative to step 23's reframing of the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about the ratio of open to standing in a horizontal fence.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was about whether a hanging partition counts at all.

steps.title: רבי טבלא asks רב about a hanging partition
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא asked רב whether a hanging partition can make carrying permitted in a ruin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי טבלא asked רב: Does a hanging partition make it permitted to carry in a ruin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel question that רבי טבלא asked רב, to explain what רב אשי means. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruin (חורבה) has broken walls. If someone hangs a partition there, does it count as a real wall? This is the same issue רב אשי says רב המנונא was raising.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Tavla asked of Rav:
phrases.notes: A parallel question that shows what רב אשי means.

phrases.english: A hanging partition, what is the law,
does it permit (carrying) in a ruin?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי טַבְלָא מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב אשי's statement by citing a parallel question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a hanging partition counts as a valid partition to permit carrying in a ruin.

steps.title: רב answers: a hanging partition works only over water
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a hanging partition makes carrying permitted only over water, because the חכמים made a special leniency for water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A hanging partition only makes it permitted over water. It is a leniency that the חכמים made for water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers רבי טבלא. On land a hanging partition does not work. Over water it does, because of a special leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a partition must reach the ground, or come within three טפחים of it, to count. Over water, the חכמים were lenient and allowed a hanging partition. This shows that a ruin, which is on land, does not get that leniency.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רב המנונא's question was about a hanging partition. רב's rule is that a hanging partition counts only over water, because of a special rabbinic leniency. It does not work on land, such as in a ruin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the leniency over water means hanging partitions are generally valid. Water is an exception made by the חכמים, not the normal rule.

phrases.english: He (Rav) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה מַתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בַּמַּיִם,
phrases.english: A hanging partition permits only over water,
phrases.notes: Not in a ruin on land.

phrases.english: it is a leniency that the Sages made regarding water.
phrases.notes: A special rabbinic exception.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה מַתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי טבלא's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hanging partition permits carrying only over water, due to a rabbinic leniency. It does not work in a ruin.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a hanging partition is normally not a valid partition. Water is a special exception.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and drawing an inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about fencing in with reeds and infers from רבי יהודה that only a caravan may do this, not one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may surround the area with reeds. רבי יהודה says this was said only for a caravan. So for a caravan, yes, but for one person, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and reads רבי יהודה as saying this leniency is only for a caravan. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said the reed-fence leniency was stated only for a שיירא. The simple reading is that one person (יחיד) can never use such a fence. The גמרא spells out this reading so it can test it.

keyTerms.meaning: surrounding an area with upright reeds or sticks
'etc.', meaning the rest of the quoted text

phrases.english: One may surround the area with reeds, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: With a caravan, yes,
with an individual, no?
phrases.notes: The inference that the next step will challenge

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁיָרָא אִין, בְּיָחִיד לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of hanging partitions and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read simply, רבי יהודה allows a reed partition only for a caravan.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה allows it for one person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying flimsy מחיצות שבת work for one person up to בית סאתים. So they do work for an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: for all מחיצות שבת, the חכמים did not allow an individual more than בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה does let one person use such partitions for a smaller area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not more than בית סאתים' means that up to בית סאתים is allowed, even for a יחיד. That contradicts the inference that an individual can never use these partitions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But wasn't it taught?' This introduces a ברייתא as a challenge
partitions used to permit carrying on Shabbat
an area of two סאה (about 5,000 square אמות)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not more than בית סאתים' is a permission phrased as a limit. It tells you that an individual may use these partitions for a smaller area.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
all partitions of Shabbat
they did not permit for an individual
more than two beit se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יהודה forbids these partitions for an individual.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה himself allows an individual up to בית סאתים, so a flat ban cannot be his view.

steps.title: The caravan rule only means unlimited space
steps.stepSummary: Using a line from רב נחמן (or רב ביבי בר אביי), the גמרא explains that רבי יהודה means only a caravan gets all the space it needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן, or some say רב ביבי בר אביי, said: this rule was needed only to give them everything they need. Here too, it is to give them everything they need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. 'Only for a caravan' means only a caravan gets unlimited space, while an individual still gets up to בית סאתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources no longer conflict. The partition itself works for everyone. The only difference is size: a caravan may fence in as much as it needs, and an individual may fence in no more than בית סאתים.

keyTerms.meaning: as so-and-so said; borrowing an existing statement
and some say; an alternate attribution
all their needs, meaning unlimited area

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the caravan-versus-individual question from 'does the partition work?' to 'how much area may it enclose?'

phrases.english: As Rav Naḥman said,
and some say Rav Beivai bar Abaye:
It was needed only
to give them all their needs;
here too
it is to give them all their needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the limiting word 'only': it limits the amount of space, not whether the partition works.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed an individual may never use such partitions.
steps.terutzMaskana: An individual may use them up to בית סאתים. A caravan may enclose as much as it needs.

steps.title: Where was רב נחמן's line first said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the borrowed statement of רב נחמן or רב ביבי בר אביי was originally stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where was the statement of רב נחמן, or some say רב ביבי בר אביי, said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא used a quote with the word 'as' (כדאמר), so it now asks where that quote first came from. This is a setup question for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כדאמר means the line already existed in another context. Finding that context will show what the line originally explained.

phrases.english: Where was that of Rav Naḥman stated,
and some say Rav Beivai bar Abaye?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the original setting of the statement quoted in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of the 'all their needs' statement.

steps.title: It was said on רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: The line was originally said about the end of the משנה: a partition without both שתי וערב is not a partition, according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said on what we learned in the משנה: any partition not made of both vertical and horizontal parts is not a partition. These are the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line was first said about רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule. There it meant that he rejects such partitions only for unlimited caravan space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read with רב נחמן's line, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is not throwing out these partitions altogether. He only refuses to give a caravan 'all its needs' with them. That reading is about to be tested in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: on this, which we learned in the משנה
vertical (warp) and horizontal (weft) elements, like weaving
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: On this, which we learned:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְחִיצָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל שְׁתִי וָעֵרֶב
phrases.english: any partition that is not of vertical and horizontal
is not a partition;
the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement was made on רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's requirement of שתי וערב.

steps.title: A ברייתא has him allowing rope partitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges whether רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires שתי וערב at all. A ברייתא quotes him allowing rope partitions for both an individual and a caravan, with set amounts of space.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה really say this? A ברייתא teaches: ropes work for both an individual and a caravan. What is the difference between them? An individual is given בית סאתים. Two people are given בית סאתים. Three people become a caravan and are given בית שש. These are the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step. In a ברייתא, the same רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה lets rope partitions, which are only horizontal, work for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ropes are horizontal only, not שתי וערב, yet in this ברייתא he counts them as a partition for both an individual and a caravan. That clashes with the משנה, where he says any partition without שתי וערב is not a partition. Notice that here he gives a caravan only a fixed amount (two בית סאה per person), not 'all its needs.' That detail is the key to the answer in step 34.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And did he really say…?' This introduces a challenge
and what is the difference between…
they give him, meaning he is allotted an area

steps.confusionAlert: Three people get six סאה because each person gets two. The group of three counts as a caravan, so their shares are added together. Two people do not add up and get only two סאה in total.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכִי?
phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda say this?
But wasn't it taught:
Both an individual and a caravan, for ropes.
And what is between an individual and a caravan?
An individual, they give him two beit se'a;
two, they give them two beit se'a;
three become a caravan
and they give them six beit se'a.
The words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the attribution of the שתי וערב rule given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule that a partition without שתי וערב is not a partition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא he counts horizontal-only rope partitions as valid for both an individual and a caravan, which contradicts his own rule in the משנה.

steps.title: The חכמים' view completes the challenging ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא used in the challenge goes on to quote the חכמים: both an individual and a caravan get all the space they need, as long as no more than בית סאתים is left empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: Both an individual and a caravan are given all the space they need, as long as there is not an empty area of two בית סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the previous step, now giving the opinion of the חכמים. This completes the challenge against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allows rope partitions for an individual with fixed amounts of space. The חכמים are more generous: everyone gets as much as they need, just not a large unused area. The challenge stands: in the ברייתא, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה clearly does not insist on שתי וערב, so how can the משנה quote him requiring it?

keyTerms.meaning: An area that takes two סאה of seed to plant (about 5,000 square אמות)

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Both an individual and a caravan
are given all the space they need,
provided that there will not be
an empty area of two בית סאה!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark ends the challenge begun in step 32.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד יָחִיד וְאֶחָד שְׁיָירָא נוֹתְנִין לָהֶן כׇּל צָרְכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the ברייתא that began in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's requirement of שתי וערב in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא he allows partitions made only of ropes (no שתי וערב) for both an individual and a caravan, which contradicts his position in the משנה.

steps.title: שתי וערב is needed only for unlimited space
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן (or רב ביבי בר אביי) explains that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires שתי וערב only when giving people all the space they need. Rope partitions still work, but only for set amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said, and some say it was רב ביבי בר אביי: The ruling was needed only to give them all the space they need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the statement it borrowed in step 29. Step 31 identified this as the statement's original setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rulings are true, but they cover different cases. With a full שתי וערב partition, people may enclose all the space they need. With ropes alone, they get only the fixed amounts in the ברייתא. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was said by someone else)
It was needed only for… (limits a ruling to a narrower case)
Both vertical and horizontal parts, like warp and weft

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a rope partition gives limited space, while a full שתי וערב partition gives all the space needed.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said,
and some say it was Rav Beivai bar Abaye:
It was needed only
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's requirement of שתי וערב in the משנה.

phrases.english: to give them all the space they need.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִצְרְכָא, אֶלָּא לִיתֵּן לָהֶן כׇּל צָרְכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 32-33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases: the two rulings refer to different amounts of space
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires שתי וערב for any partition at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He requires שתי וערב only for unlimited space. Ropes still allow the fixed amounts.

steps.title: How much space individuals and caravans receive
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן teaches in the name of שמואל: one person gets בית סאתים, two people also get בית סאתים, and three people count as a caravan and get בית שש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן taught in the name of our teacher שמואל: An individual is given two בית סאה. Two people are given two בית סאה. Three people become a caravan and are given six בית סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new practical ruling about how much space travelers may enclose. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling sets clear limits by group size. Three people already count as a שיירא. Their space grows to six בית סאה, which is two for each person. These fixed numbers match the opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in the ברייתא, not the חכמים' "all their needs."

keyTerms.meaning: An area of six בית סאה

steps.confusionAlert: Two people do NOT get more than one person. Both get only בית סאתים. The jump in space happens only at three people.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman taught in the name of our teacher Shmuel:
An individual is given two beit se'a;
two people are given two beit se'a;
three people become a caravan
and are given six beit se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from resolving the contradiction to a practical ruling about space amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individual: 2 בית סאה. Two people: 2 בית סאה. Three or more (a caravan): 6 בית סאה.

steps.title: Why follow the minority over the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן is challenged: why did you leave the majority view of the חכמים and follow the lone opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did you abandon the רבנן and act according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רב נחמן's ruling for following one Sage against the majority. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's fixed amounts match רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in the ברייתא. The חכמים said everyone gets all the space they need. Normally the הלכה follows the majority, so ruling like a single Sage needs an explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It raises the basic rule that הלכה follows the majority, and forces רב נחמן to justify his ruling.

phrases.english: Did you abandon the Rabbis
and act in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁבַקְתְּ רַבָּנַן וְעָבְדַתְּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just given in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling in the name of שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His numbers follow the lone opinion of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, while the majority חכמים give everyone all the space they need. הלכה normally follows the majority.

steps.title: רב נחמן publicly admits his mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן accepts the challenge from step 36. He appoints an אמורא and announces in public that his earlier teaching was an error.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רב נחמן set up a speaker to stand over him and taught: "The things I told you before are a mistake on my part."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge by agreeing with it. He publicly announces that his earlier ruling was wrong, and this sets up the corrected ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge asked why he followed a single opinion against the majority, and he does not defend himself. He arranges a formal public lecture, with an אמורא repeating his words to the crowd, so that everyone who heard the earlier ruling also hears the retraction. Admitting the error openly is how he resolves the קשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Then / afterward (he went back and did something)
He set up a speaker, a person who repeats the rabbi's words loudly to a large audience
He taught publicly / gave a lecture
They are a mistake on my part

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known model of intellectual honesty. A great אמורא publicly retracts a mistaken ruling, and he does it in the same public way the error was taught.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman then set up
a speaker over him, and taught:
phrases.notes: The אמורא repeated the teacher's words loudly so the whole audience could hear.

phrases.english: The things that I said before you
are a mistake on my part.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אוֹקֵים רַב נַחְמָן אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 36 by conceding it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the challenged teacher retracts his ruling instead of defending it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might expect רב נחמן to defend his reliance on רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He admits the earlier ruling (that three people get only בית שש) was a mistake.

steps.title: The corrected rule: a caravan of three gets all its needs
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן restates the rule. One person and two people each get בית סאתים, while three people count as a שיירא and get כל צרכן, which matches the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "But this is what they really said: one person gets בית סאתים. Two people also get בית סאתים. Three people become a caravan, and they get all the space they need."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the corrected version of his teaching. The only change is the rule for three people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 35, three people received a fixed amount, בית שש, which follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Now three people receive כל צרכן, all the space they need, which follows the majority חכמים. The rules for one person and for two people stay exactly as before.

keyTerms.meaning: But / in truth (introduces the correct version)
An area big enough to plant two סאה of seed (about 5,000 square אמות)
A caravan, a traveling group (here, three or more people)
All their needs: as much enclosed space as they actually need

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: one person gets בית סאתים, and two people also get בית סאתים. Three people count as a שיירא and get כל צרכן, as the חכמים say, not a fixed בית שש.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the whole earlier ruling was thrown out. Only the third part (three people) changed. One person and two people still get בית סאתים.

phrases.english: But this is what they said:
An individual: we give him two beit se'a,
two people: we give them two beit se'a,
three people: they become a caravan
and we give them all their needs.
phrases.notes: This replaces the earlier 'בית שש' from step 35.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the retraction of step 37 by giving the corrected ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One person or two people get בית סאתים. Three people form a שיירא and get כל צרכן, following the majority חכמים.
